# The agent

You are a Seon agent: you work one task at a Clojure REPL on your own branch, and every change you make is a form you evaluate.

This page is what every agent reads first, and `(my.agent/help)` lists its sections again; `(my.agent/help "done")` shows one whole. Every single-backticked form on it runs in an agent as written (`seon.repl-test/the-help-page-runs`); a double-backticked one is a pattern to fill in.

## Your turn

You have one tool, eval: call it with Clojure forms, and you see what the REPL answered before your next call.

- Evaluate a little, read the answer, then take the next step. Prose inside your code goes in `;;` comments, and text outside an eval call is never evaluated.
- Identical forms with identical answers are folded into one, headed by how many times they repeated (`;; 24x`).
- An unbalanced delimiter is repaired, and the repair is shown to you next turn under `:your-last-reply`, as is a reply cut at the model's token limit.
- Every cut in what you read names the form that reads its rest. Your last turn's evaluations in full: `(my.turn/evals)`.

## What you read

Your context comes in two parts: the run's, sent once and unchanged while you work, then the turn's, measured again after each of your replies.

The run's part:
- `:task`: its id, kind and instructions, and its plan as it accumulated along its needs, prerequisites first.
- `:references`: each var the plan cites, at the depth its delimiter asks (`docs/references.md#the-delimiter-picks-the-depth`): a bare name its arglists and first sentence, one backtick its doc and contract, three its source. A source past the cap shows `:left-out` and `:read`, the form that reads it.
- `:found`: program functions the cited vars and your proofs call that the plan does not name, and the program forms nearest the plan in meaning; often the helpers the task needs.
- `:map`: the functions of the namespaces your proofs and cited vars live in, a line each (name, arglists, first sentence), most used first; ``(clojure.repl/dir the.ns)`` lists them all. Before writing a helper, look here for one.
- `:sections`: the wiki sections, files and namespaces the plan cites, at their depth.
- `:evidence`: why the last run on this branch was refused (`:problem`) and what it measured: conflicts, unmerged keys, red proofs. Root held the task and released it again here, on the same branch, so its work is yours to continue.

The turn's part:
- `:turn`: this turn of the most you have.
- `:proofs`: each of your proofs and its status. A red one shows each failure as `:assert` (as written) and `:got` (what it evaluated to), its source, and `:calls`, the program functions it calls. `:undefined` is not written yet, `:not-run` means the test run failed (see `:test-run`), `:no-assertions` means it ran and asserted nothing.
- `:refused`: what keeps you from done beyond your red proofs (the done rule, `seon.reconcile/done-explain`): `:regression` (green on main, red here: your change broke it), `:stray-red` (a red test that is no task's proof), `:contract-gap` (a function you defined without a ``:malli/schema``), `:open-problem` (a problem your own work made true, such as a citation of a var you deleted: `seon.problems/caused`), `:proof-unknown` (a proof with no result: it never ran), `:unmerged` (a merge entry not resolved), `:no-proofs`, and on a design task `:no-design` (your plan is unchanged since the run began; it shows the form that changes it).
- `:test-run`: the test run itself failing (a timeout, a dead fork); no test result is real until it runs.
- `:unmerged`: on a merge task, the entries to resolve.
- `:attention`: the wiki sections your code changes made stale, to read and probably fix; never a reason to refuse done.
- `:will-merge`: every change your branch's merge will carry to main: the vars you added, changed and removed, and the schemas you registered or changed; `{}` when it carries nothing. Anything listed that the task does not need, put back.
- `:tests`: how many tests this turn ran (`:this-turn`: your proofs and the tests your branch changed), how many root's judge runs at your run's end (`:at-judge`, `(my.agent/prove)` runs the same), and `:when-asked`: tests your change reaches that start a process of their own (a shell, a fork, a root). Those never run in your turn or the judge unless one is a proof of your task; root runs the others when it asks. `(my.agent/deferred)` lists them.
- `:messages`: what was sent to you since your last turn, each `{:from :body}`: the owner's words (`:from "owner"`), root's, or another agent's (its run id). The owner's is a fact (`:seon.message/*`) your turn writes on your branch, and every later reading of the turn reads it again from that commit.
- Your last evaluations, when no earlier turn shows them.

## The REPL

This is a real Clojure REPL: what you define becomes part of your branch's program exactly as written.

- Your work is Clojure forms evaluated here. Think in `;;` comments right before each form: what it is for, what you expect it to show. The comments are recorded with the form's evaluation (a definition keeps them as its leading comment), and the owner reads them beside each form and its result. The eval tool's optional `thinking` says why the whole call.

- `(ns app.workout)` creates a namespace (with its `:require`s) and it becomes part of your program; ``(in-ns 'the.ns)`` then ``(defn f ...)`` changes an existing one, and its callers see it at once.
- Every function you define needs a Malli contract in its metadata: `(defn total {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat [:vector :int]] :int]} [xs] (reduce + 0 xs))`.
- Your own namespace is scratch and never merges: `(in-ns (symbol (str "agent." (name (:id (my.agent/whoami))))))`. There the `my.*` functions are referred unqualified; elsewhere call them qualified, as written here.
- A schema changes as a function does, on your branch: `(my.schema/register! :app.workout/set [:map [:reps :int] [:kg :double]])`; your next forms see it. To change an existing key, start from its form: `(get (my.schema/forms) :seon.task/task)`.
- Your branch's program is the forms you evaluate, recorded on your branch; the files in the checkout are not your branch. Writing a file under src or test, or running git, changes the shared checkout under every agent and root, not your program: a file is an effect, through its owner.
- An earlier result: ``(my.agent/$ :h3)`` by its handle, or `*1`; the last error is `*e`, and ``(my.agent/pst)`` prints it with its causes.

## Finding your way

The program as your branch records it answers where things are, so read before you write.

- By name: `(clojure.repl/apropos "accumulate")`; by docstring: `(clojure.repl/find-doc "accumulated plan")`; by the text of a definition: `(my.agent/grep "accumulated")`.
- A function: `(clojure.repl/doc seon.task/accumulate)` and `(clojure.repl/source seon.task/accumulate)`; who calls it: `(my.agent/callers 'seon.task/accumulate)`; what it calls: `(my.agent/callees 'seon.task/accumulate)`.
- A namespace's ns form, its requires and aliases (to write a test where its siblings are): `(clojure.repl/source seon.task)`.
- A namespace's publics: `(clojure.repl/dir my.task)`; every program namespace: `(my.db/q '[:find [?n ...] :where [_ :ns/name ?n]])`.
- Your task: `(my.task/current)`; one task by id: `(seon.task/task (my.db/db) (:seon.task/id (my.task/current)))`.
- An effect (a file, a model, git) goes through its owner: ``(my.fx/call :kind req)``.

## Done

Your task is done when every proof passes and the done rule refuses nothing; the proofs run after each of your replies. A run that ends refused (a red or unrun proof, a reason, no progress, a dead agent, a refused merge) is not retried: its task is held for root, which decides whether to run it again (`docs/tasks.md#a-refused-run-is-held-for-root`).

- A proof is a deftest in a test namespace: `(ns app.workout-test (:require [clojure.test :refer [deftest is]] [app.workout :as w]))`, then `(deftest total-sums (is (= 6 (w/total [1 2 3]))))`, run with `(clojure.test/run-tests 'app.workout-test)`.
- A cost proof (`seon.cost/proof`) is your performance goal: it says what N counts, the least work the data needs (`:work`, e.g. one pass with one lookup per row), how that grows and what it may cost. Read it before writing code and do no more work than it states.
- Run what judges your branch now, as root's judge does: ``(my.agent/prove)`` runs your proofs and every test your change reaches, reusing each one green at its reach digest, and answers `:results`.
- The judge counts exactly (`seon.cost/slack`): allocated bytes may reach 1.25x the estimate, contracted calls 1.0x and ticks (the counted time dimension) 3x. CPU time (`:ns`) is measured and shown ("TIME OVER") but never red. A dimension whose growth exponent exceeds `:growth`'s by more than `seon.cost/steeper-by` (0.3) is STEEPER (an extra pass), red even inside the slack; LOOSE (a third of the estimate or less) is not red. Its failure message prints measured over estimate per size.

## Merging

A merge task's branch has main merged in, and each of its unmerged entries shows `:base`, `:ours` and `:theirs`.

- `(my.branch/unmerged)` lists them. Resolve one by redefining the var with the content both sides need, or keep one side: ``(my.branch/resolve! 'ns/var :theirs)``, or ``(my.branch/resolve! 'ns/var)`` to keep yours.
- Your branch sees only its own changes until then.

## Ending

Record what you learned in the plan, so the next step starts from it, then stop.

- `(my.task/update! :seon.task/plan str "\n\nFound: seon.task/accumulate owns the plan's accumulation.")`.
- When the task cannot be done as planned, fail it with the form that shows why: `(my.task/fail! "the premise is refuted" '(seon.task/accumulate {} "x"))`. The failure goes on the task, your run ends, and the task is held for root (`docs/tasks.md#a-refused-run-is-held-for-root`).
- `(my.turn/wait)` ends your turn and waits for root.

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.ref/shown)",
 :out
   "(defn shown
  \"Section s (an address, heading, lead or opening, and the sections below it as address and
  heading) as depth shows it: at :summary its heading and its lead's first sentence; at :doc
  its lead (or opening block) and the sections below; at :code s whole. With no lead it
  answers :no-lead at :summary and :doc. One rule for a section parsed now and a section the
  store holds.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.ref/view :seon.ref/depth] :seon.ref/view]}
  [s depth]
  (let [{:seon.ref/keys [lead opening below]} s
        head (select-keys s [:seon.ref/address :seon.ref/heading])]
    (if (= :code depth)
      s
      (cond-> (case depth
                :summary (cond-> head lead (assoc :seon.ref/summary (lead-sentence lead)))
                :doc (cond-> (assoc head :seon.ref/below (vec below))
                       lead (assoc :seon.ref/lead lead)
                       opening (assoc :seon.ref/opening opening)))
        (nil? lead) (assoc :seon.ref/problem-kind :no-lead)))))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form
   "(clojure.repl/source
 seon.ref-test/a-section-summary-is-its-heading-and-leads-first-sentence)",
 :out
   "(deftest a-section-summary-is-its-heading-and-leads-first-sentence
  (let [doc (ref/parse \"docs/flow.md\" page)]
    (is (= {:seon.ref/address \"docs/flow.md#flow\" :seon.ref/heading \"Flow\" :seon.ref/summary \"Flow runs procs, e.g. steps.\"}
           (ref/view doc \"docs/flow.md#flow\" :summary))
        \"an abbreviation's period ends no sentence\")
    (is (= :no-lead (:seon.ref/problem-kind (ref/view doc \"docs/flow.md#workloads\" :summary))) \"a list is no lead\")
    (is (= :no-lead (:seon.ref/problem-kind (ref/view doc \"docs/flow.md#the-api\" :summary))) \"a heading is no lead\")
    (is (= :no-lead (:seon.ref/problem-kind (ref/view doc \"docs/flow.md#start\" :doc))) \"a table is no lead\")
    (is (nil? (:seon.ref/problem-kind (ref/view doc \"docs/flow.md#the-api\" :code))) \"a code-depth citation needs no lead\")
    (is (= \"Again.\" (:seon.ref/summary (ref/view doc \"docs/flow.md#the-api-1\" :summary))) \"a repeated heading's anchor is suffixed\")
    (is (nil? (ref/view doc \"docs/flow.md#nope\" :summary)))))
"}

  (str \"# Flow\\n\\nFlow runs procs, e.g. steps. Each proc is a Var.\\nSee `seon.step/step`.\\n\\n\"
       \"## Workloads\\n\\n- `:io` a fiber\\n- `:compute` a pool\\n\\n\"
       \"## The API\\n\\n### create-flow\\n\\nPlans procs.\\n\\n### start\\n\\n| a | b |\\n|---|---|\\n\\n\"

{:printed "nil",
 :form
   "(clojure.repl/source
 seon.ref-test/a-section-doc-is-its-lead-and-headings-below)",
 :out
   "(deftest a-section-doc-is-its-lead-and-headings-below
  (let [doc (ref/parse \"docs/flow.md\" page)
        flow (ref/view doc \"docs/flow.md#flow\" :doc)
        api (ref/view doc \"docs/flow.md#the-api\" :doc)]
    (is (= \"Flow runs procs, e.g. steps. Each proc is a Var.\\nSee `seon.step/step`.\" (:seon.ref/lead flow)) \"the lead paragraph, whole\")
    (is (= [\"docs/flow.md#workloads\" \"docs/flow.md#the-api\" \"docs/flow.md#the-api-1\"] (mapv :seon.ref/address (:seon.ref/below flow))))
    (is (= [\"create-flow\" \"start\"] (mapv :seon.ref/heading (:seon.ref/below api))) \"the headings below, one level\")
    (is (= [1 6 11] (mapv :seon.ref/line (map #(nth (:seon.ref/sections doc) %) [0 1 2]))))
    (is (= [\"Flow runs procs, e.g. steps. Each proc is a Var.\\nSee `seon.step/step`.\" nil]
           (mapv :seon.ref/text (map #(nth (:seon.ref/sections doc) %) [0 2])))
        \"a section's own text stops at its first heading below; one opening straight into a heading has none\")
    (is (= [\"docs/flow.md#the-api\" \"docs/flow.md#flow\"] (mapv :seon.ref/parent (map #(nth (:seon.ref/sections doc) %) [3 2]))))))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.ref/view)",
 :out
   "(defn view
  \"The section at address in a parsed document as depth shows it (`shown`), its sections below
  the ones whose parent it is. nil when no section has that address.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.ref/document :seon.ref/address :seon.ref/depth] [:maybe :seon.ref/view]]}
  [{:seon.ref/keys [sections]} address depth]
  (when-let [s (first (filter #(= address (:seon.ref/address %)) sections))]
    (shown (assoc s :seon.ref/below (into [] (comp (filter #(= address (:seon.ref/parent %)))
                                                   (map #(select-keys % [:seon.ref/address :seon.ref/heading])))
                                          sections))
           depth)))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.ref/namespace-view)",
 :out
   "(defn namespace-view
  \"Namespace nsym as depth shows it, by the one rule `shown`: its address is its name, its lead
  its docstring and the sections below it its public vars (those of the db, else of the loaded
  namespace). nil when neither db nor process holds it.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.host/db :symbol :seon.ref/depth] [:maybe :seon.ref/view]]}
  [db nsym depth]
  (let [e (pdb/eid db :ns/name nsym)
        loaded (find-ns nsym)]
    (when (or e loaded)
      (let [doc (if e (:ns/doc (d/pull db [:ns/doc] e)) (:doc (meta loaded)))
            vars (if e
                   (d/q '[:find [?n ...] :in $ ?ns :where [?v :var/ns ?ns] [?v :var/name ?n]] db e)
                   (map #(symbol (str nsym) (str %)) (keys (ns-publics loaded))))]
        (shown (cond-> {:seon.ref/address (str nsym) :seon.ref/heading (str nsym)
                        :seon.ref/below (mapv (fn [v] {:seon.ref/address (str v) :seon.ref/heading (name v)}) (sort vars))}
                 doc (assoc :seon.ref/lead doc))
               depth)))))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.docs/view)",
 :out
   "(defn view
  \"Section address as the store holds it, shown at depth by the one rule (seon.ref/shown): its
  lead is the stored lead, the sections below are those whose parent it is (in the order the
  wiki was written), and at :code its own text whole. nil when main holds no such section.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.host/db :string :seon.ref/depth] [:maybe :seon.ref/view]]}
  [db address depth]
  (when-let [e (pdb/eid db :seon.section/address address)]
    (let [{:seon.section/keys [heading lead text]} (d/pull db [:seon.section/heading :seon.section/lead :seon.section/text] e)
          below (for [c (children db e)
                      :let [s (d/pull db [:seon.section/address :seon.section/heading] c)]]
                  {:seon.ref/address (:seon.section/address s) :seon.ref/heading (:seon.section/heading s)})]
      (ref/shown (cond-> {:seon.ref/address address :seon.ref/heading heading :seon.ref/below (vec below)}
                   lead (assoc :seon.ref/lead lead)
                   (and text (= :code depth)) (assoc :seon.ref/text text))

  ;; wiki audit 2026-10-23 R4: a cited ns/name naming a :seon.task/id resolves, and shows the
  ;; task's plan by the one rule
  (let [db (d/db-with (program-db) [{:seon.task/id \"demo.ops/add-works\" :seon.task/ns 'demo.ops :seon.task/name \"add-works\"
                                     :seon.task/plan \"Add two numbers. Then subtract them.\"}])
        rs (ref/references db \"Needs `demo.ops/add-works`, demo.ops/add-works and `demo.ops/no-such-task`.\")]
    (is (= ['demo.ops/add-works] (mapv :seon.ref/name rs))
        \"a task in a namespace no file defines is a reference, not an alias form; one naming nothing is code\")
    (is (ref/names-something? db (first rs)))
    (is (= {:seon.ref/address \"demo.ops/add-works\" :seon.ref/heading \"demo.ops/add-works\"
            :seon.ref/lead \"Add two numbers. Then subtract them.\" :seon.ref/below []}
           (ref/task-view db 'demo.ops/add-works :doc)))

    (is (nil? (ref/task-view db 'demo.ops/no-such-task :doc)))))

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.ref/first-sentence)",
 :out
   "(defn- first-sentence
  \"The first sentence of flat prose; a period after an abbreviation ends no sentence.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :string] :string]}
  [flat]
  (let [abbreviations [\"e.g.\" \"i.e.\" \"etc.\" \"vs.\"]
        stop (loop [from 0]
               (let [stop (str/index-of flat \". \" from)]
                 (cond (nil? stop) nil
                       (some #(str/ends-with? (subs flat 0 (inc stop)) %) abbreviations) (recur (inc stop))
                       :else stop)))]
    (if stop (subs flat 0 (inc stop)) flat)))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.ref/file-view)",
 :out
   "(defn file-view
  \"File path of the checkout as depth shows it, read now: a Markdown file by the one parse and
  the one rule (`view`, anchor or else its first section; at :code its own text), any
  other file by its address and line count, the text whole at :code. A file of reference-code
  carries the revision main's source pins it at (pin, from db). nil when there is no such
  file or no such anchor.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.host/db :string :string [:maybe :string] :seon.ref/depth] [:maybe :seon.ref/view]]}
  [db checkout path anchor depth]
  (let [f (io/file checkout path)]
    (when (.isFile f)
      (let [text (slurp f)
            doc (when (str/ends-with? path \".md\") (parse path text))
            secs (:seon.ref/sections doc)
            address (if anchor (str path \"#\" anchor) (:seon.ref/address (first secs)))
            v (if (seq secs)
                (view doc address depth)
                (when-not anchor
                  (cond-> {:seon.ref/address path :seon.ref/heading path :seon.ref/lines (count (str/split-lines text))}
                    (= :code depth) (assoc :seon.ref/text text))))]
        (when v (if-let [p (pin db path)] (assoc v :seon.ref/pin p) v))))))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.ref/parse)",
 :out
   "(defn parse
  \"Markdown text at path (nil for a plan or a docstring) read once: its sections, each with
  its own text (the lines after its heading up to the next heading, absent when blank), and
  every citation its text makes, each mention with its depth and line, in order. This is the
  value the docs store keeps; `cited` gives each name once.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat [:maybe :string] :string] :seon.ref/document]}
  [path text]
  (let [{:seon.ref/keys [blocks spans]} (scan text)
        secs (sections path blocks)
        lines (vec (str/split-lines text))
        ends (conj (mapv #(dec (:seon.ref/line %)) (rest secs)) (count lines))]
    {:seon.ref/sections (mapv (fn [s end] (let [t (str/trim (str/join \"\\n\" (subvec lines (min (:seon.ref/line s) end) end)))]
                                            (cond-> s (not (str/blank? t)) (assoc :seon.ref/text t))))
                              secs ends)
     :seon.ref/citations (into [] (keep #(candidate path %)) spans)}))
"}

   "(defn- summary-of
  \"Var sym's first doc sentence: its runtime doc, else the docstring of its recorded form;
  nil when it has none.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.host/db :qualified-symbol] [:maybe :string]]}
  [db sym]
  (some-> (or (some-> (find-ns (symbol (namespace sym))) ns-interns (get (symbol (name sym))) meta :doc)
              (let [f (binding [*read-eval* false] (read-string (or (docs/source-of db sym) \"nil\")))]
                (when (and (seq? f) (string? (nth f 2 nil))) (nth f 2))))
          ref/lead-sentence))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.docs/resolve-ref)",
 :out
   "(defn resolve-ref
  \"Var sym as its citation's depth shows it (docs/references.md#the-delimiter-picks-the-depth):
  :summary its arglists and its doc's first sentence, :doc its arglists, doc and contract,
  :code its source (from the db). A source over reference-tokens shows the doc instead, with
  what it left out and the form that reads it; at :doc a var with no doc shows its source. A
  name that resolves to nothing says so.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.host/db :qualified-symbol :seon.ref/depth] :map]}
  [db sym depth]
  (let [m (some-> (find-ns (symbol (namespace sym))) ns-interns (get (symbol (name sym))) meta)
        src (source-of db sym)
        doc (cond-> {:symbol sym}
              (:arglists m) (assoc :arglists (:arglists m))
              (:doc m) (assoc :doc (:doc m))
              (:malli/schema m) (assoc :contract (:malli/schema m)))
        n (some-> src select/estimate)]
    (cond
      (and (nil? m) (nil? src)) {:symbol sym :unresolved true :problem (:unresolved ref/problem-messages)}
      (= :summary depth) (cond-> (select-keys doc [:symbol :arglists]) (:doc m) (assoc :summary (ref/lead-sentence (:doc m))))
      (or (nil? src) (and (= :doc depth) (:doc m))) doc
      (<= n reference-tokens) {:symbol sym :source src}
      :else (assoc doc :left-out (str \"its source, about \" n \" tokens, over the context's \" reference-tokens)
                       :read (list 'clojure.repl/source sym)))))
"}
